text:
aven't committed anything; the changes are uncommitted in `worktree-world`. The completion file is written as `completed`.

## Checks I ran
- `npm ci`: ok.
- `npm run typecheck`: passes.
- `npm run test:unit`: 548 pass.
- `npm run test:integration`: 37 pass.
- `npm run build`, including the smoke test: passes.
- Full Playwright suite with the JSON reporter: 6 passed, and `check-report` says the report follows the verifier's rules.
- `tests/e2e/sea.spec.ts --repeat-each=5`: 10 of 10 passed, so `sail-and-dock` passed 5 in a row. The machine's load average was 6–8 during the run.

## What changed
- **Map:** 111 × 111 tiles, generated from an ASCII sketch of one quarter that is mirrored into all four (`assets/source/maps/sketch.ts` writes `slice-sea.tmj`). There is one island per quarter, plus reefs, and shoal walls on the midlines that open only near a new `hub` point in the centre. `npm run map:build` reports:
  - neighbouring islands 26.4 s apart;
  - longest crossing 39.3 s;
  - every spawn slot within 7.3 s of a dock;
  - no open water more than 9.9 tiles from an obstacle;
  - 90.7 % open sea.
- **Two new validators:** one checks that no open water is farther than the sight radius from land, a shoal or a dock. The other checks that every route between docks on different islands passes through the hub's disc. Each is shown failing on a broken map in `maps.test.ts`.
- **Ship tuning:**

  | | Now | Before |
  |---|---|---|
  | maxSpeed | 39 | 64 |
  | acceleration | 3 | 4 |
  | braking | 3 | 8 |
  | drag | 1 | 2 |
  | reverse speed | 10 | 16 |
  | reverse acceleration | 1 | 2 |
  | dock speed | 15 | 24 |

  The dock reach stays at 384. Simulation tests compare time to full speed, stopping distance, the 3.2 s full turn and the turning circle in pixels against the old tuning at 16 px; all are within 25 %.
- **Drawing scale:** tiles are 24 px, and the Tiled map uses the same size, so a single `TILE_PIXELS` constant covers both. A web test checks that the sight circle fits the view and that the camera clamp uses the map's size.
- **Keyboard:** a quick tap of E is now kept until the page's next read. A web unit test shows that a tap between two reads docks the ship.
- **Test positions:** all come from the map, mostly a clear row three tiles south of the hub, and every leg is checked for a clear hull-width line. The test placement route now builds its tile limits from the map (`createTestPlacementSchema`).
- **`sail-and-dock`:** the ship stops two tiles east and three out, turns to heading 46 or 47, then holds ahead and E into the corner of the shore. A simulation test tries starting points every 16 sub-units across the three tiles east of the dock, 2–4 tiles out, and each one moors.

## Things you should know
- **`sailTo` works differently now.** Steering continuously failed under load because the HUD lagged by 1–2 s. It now moves in hops: it turns at rest, holds ahead for a number of steps worked out from the ship tuning, then coasts to a stop. It never brakes.
- **I found a game edge case and didn't fix it (out of scope).** If the page stalls for more than 250 ms, the server treats the input as released and forgets which throttle the ship moored with. A moored ship then casts off if ahead is still held after E is let go. The browser test lets go of ahead before E to avoid it.
- **Rocks weren't added** (optional item 4); all new obstacles are shoals.
- **The out-of-sight ships don't cross the vertical wall's gap.** They sit on the clear row just east of the gap, 13 tiles apart, with open water to the south to turn in, because the guest ran into the wall when I placed them on either side of the gap.
- **Worth checking by playing:** whether sending every route between islands through the one crossing at the centre feels like ships meeting rather than a bottleneck, and whether 24 px tiles read well. No automated check covers that.

To regenerate the map after editing the sketch: `node assets/source/maps/sketch.ts && npm run map:build`.
